name: Jude
description: Urgent warning · failed promises · restrained speech · mercy · keeping power

1.text: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to those who are called, sanctified by God the Father, and kept for Jesus Christ:
May mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you.

Beloved, while I was very eager to write to you about our common salvation, I was constrained to write to you exhorting you to contend earnestly for the faith which was once for all delivered to the saints.

For there are certain men who crept in secretly, even those who were long ago written about for this condemnation: ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into indecency, and denying our only Master, God, and Lord, Jesus Christ.
Now I desire to remind you, though you already know this, that the Lord, having saved a people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who didn’t believe.
Angels who didn’t keep their first domain, but deserted their own dwelling place, he has kept in everlasting bonds under darkness for the judgment of the great day.

Even as Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them, having in the same way as these given themselves over to sexual immorality and gone after strange flesh, are shown as an example, suffering the punishment of eternal fire.
Yet in the same way, these also in their dreaming defile the flesh, despise authority, and slander celestial beings.
But Michael, the archangel, when contending with the devil and arguing about the body of Moses, dared not bring against him an abusive condemnation, but said, “May the Lord rebuke you!”
But these speak evil of whatever things they don’t know. They are destroyed in these things that they understand naturally, like the creatures without reason.
Woe to them! For they went in the way of Cain, and ran riotously in the error of Balaam for hire, and perished in Korah’s rebellion.

These are hidden rocky reefs in your love feasts when they feast with you, shepherds who without fear feed themselves; clouds without water, carried along by winds; autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots;
wild waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, for whom the blackness of darkness has been reserved forever.
About these also Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied, saying, “Behold, the Lord came with ten thousands of his holy ones,

to execute judgment on all, and to convict all the ungodly of all their works of ungodliness which they have done in an ungodly way, and of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.”
These are murmurers and complainers, walking after their lusts—and their mouth speaks proud things—showing respect of persons to gain advantage.
But you, beloved, remember the words which have been spoken before by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ.
They said to you, “In the last time there will be mockers, walking after their own ungodly lusts.”
These are those who cause divisions and are sensual, not having the Spirit.
But you, beloved, keep building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit.
Keep yourselves in God’s love, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ to eternal life.
On some have compassion, making a distinction,
and some save, snatching them out of the fire with fear, hating even the clothing stained by the flesh.
Now to him who is able to keep them from stumbling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory in great joy,
to God our Savior, who alone is wise, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and forever. Amen.

chapters.title: An urgent warning ends with mercy and confidence in God's keeping power
chapters.summary: Jude, brother of James, writes to those who are called. He urges them to contend for the faith delivered to the saints. Certain people have crept in and turn God’s grace into license. He recalls Israel in the wilderness, the angels who left their place, and Sodom. He says the archangel Michael did not bring an abusive charge against the devil. He quotes a prophecy of Enoch about judgment. The readers should build themselves up in faith, pray, and wait for mercy. He ends with praise to God, who can keep them from stumbling.
chapters.meaning: Most of the letter condemns the people who crept in (verses 4–16). Verses 20–21 turn to the readers’ own faith, prayer, and waiting. Verse 22 then turns to how the readers treat others. It asks for compassion and for “making a distinction.” Not everyone is treated the same way. Verse 23 names a second group to be saved with fear, snatched from the fire. Verse 24 says who finally keeps anyone from stumbling: God.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson joins Jude's warning images with prayer and compassion. Why does a warning about harmful teaching end with mercy and rescue?

chapters.historicalNote: Jude changes his intended subject because he sees grace being turned into permission for wrongdoing. The USCCB introduction reads that change as an urgent warning about danger from false teachers. Recalled judgments challenge the assumption that earlier rescue removes later accountability. Michael's restrained reply contrasts with abusive speech, while clouds and fruitless trees expose failed promises. The commands then turn toward building faith, prayer, mercy, and rescue rather than accusation alone. Closing praise returns to God's keeping power, placing the warning within hope of being preserved.

people.name: Jude
people.role: Named speaker who changes his intended subject to warn against harmful teaching
people.relations: He identifies himself as a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James.
people.meaning: His final commands join protection of received faith with mercy toward people in danger.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jesus Christ
people.role: Lord whose mercy remains the ground of hope for eternal life
people.relations: Jude identifies himself as his servant and warns against denying him.
people.meaning: Waiting for his mercy belongs beside active care and prayer.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Moses
people.role: Person recalled through the dispute about his body
people.relations: Jude describes Michael's restrained reply during a dispute with the devil.
people.meaning: His mention serves a comparison about speech rather than locating his grave.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Cain
people.role: Recalled figure whose way supplies a negative comparison
people.relations: Jude places his way beside Balaam's error and Korah's rebellion.
people.meaning: The comparison joins wrongdoing with the broader warning about present conduct.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Balaam
people.role: Figure recalled through error connected with payment
people.relations: His example stands among the warning's three named comparisons.
people.meaning: Desire for gain helps explain why claimed spiritual standing does not ensure sound conduct.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Korah
people.role: Figure recalled through rebellion and destruction
people.relations: His remembered rebellion stands beside Cain and Balaam.
people.meaning: His mention connects the present warning with the consequences of earlier rebellion.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Enoch
people.role: Figure to whom Jude attributes a saying about coming judgment
people.relations: Jude calls him the seventh from Adam and quotes the judgment saying.
people.meaning: His attributed words strengthen the warning without supplying a complete account of their earlier transmission.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Adam
people.role: Ancestor named in the description of Enoch
people.relations: Jude uses his name to place Enoch within an ancestral sequence.
people.meaning: His brief mention identifies the recalled speaker rather than developing a creation account.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
